tag: Episode 5 · The Selves on My Side
title: The Selves on My Side

beats.t: The air in the mirror corridor grew heavy. Yeoni had barely dried off after the Abyss of Hae Water. Yet the reflected Yeoni before them was already raising a hand.
Countless mirror shards rose behind the reflection. Each held a different face of Yeoni.
Angry Yeoni. Giving-up Yeoni. Yeoni comparing themself to others. Yeoni smiling as though everything was fine. Yeoni with a face that said they could do nothing.
And yet another Yeoni, looking thoroughly sick of watching all those selves.
Wow. I have more release versions than I thought. Someone should have tidied up the updates.
This is the final trial on the Island of Companions.
At least tell me the name of the test. Let me prepare myself before I die.
At that moment, words appeared in the center of the corridor.

[ Island of Companions · Final Trial ]
[ Distinguish those who share your face. ]
[ Make Friends your allies; sever Rob Wealth. ]
Hold on. Why this sudden difficulty spike with no tutorial?
When energy like yours supports you, it takes the face of Friend. When it covets your share, it takes the face of Rob Wealth. Here, you must see that difference yourself.
So they both have my face, but one's on my side and the other's a fraud trying to steal my place?
Yes. But both wear your face. Don't be fooled by appearances.
Wow, innovative game design. Enemies and allies use the same skin. Would it kill you to add friendly-fire protection?
Yeoni scanned the mirror shards. Every face was theirs. Every expression too. Their throat grew dry. What were they supposed to use to tell them apart?
It won't be easy.
The reflected Yeoni snapped their fingers lightly. Click.
The angry-faced Yeoni came forward first. Arms folded, foot tapping the ground, glaring.
“You always hold everything in, then explode too late over the wrong thing.”
Hey. Opening with a brutal truth is cheating.
“You could say you don't like something right there. Instead, you act fine, then go home and kick your blankets alone.”
Stop. I just came out of the abyss after swallowing all that water. My mental state is still soggy.
“So you're going to cover it with another joke?” Yeoni shut their mouth. A reply stuck in their throat.
In the gap left by Yeoni's silence, black mirror fragments grew like thorns beneath the angry self's feet.
Careful. Now it is trying to take your share too.
Wasn't that one on my side? Everything it just said was true.
It is cornering you with truths so it can take your place. That is Rob Wealth.
Angry Yeoni smiled sharply. “So I'll speak for you. You can't do it anyway.”
Red glass fragments shot from those fingertips like arrows. Yeongnyangi sprang up to block them. Clang!
Yeoni, pull yourself together!
I know, I know!
Yeoni planted their hooves firmly. The energy of [乙] warmed their chest. Green vines sprouted beneath their feet.
But Angry Yeoni did not stop. “You're always late. Late getting angry, late speaking up, late making every decision.”
Yeoni clenched their teeth. It hurt more because it was not wrong. A hot pressure tightened beneath their ribs.
But this time, they did not want to turn and run.
...You're right. I blow up too late a lot. I won't deny it.
Angry Yeoni's eyes wavered, as though that answer had been unexpected.
But I don't want you exploding for me.
Because then those aren't my words. There's a voice, but I'm not in it.
Yeoni stepped into the path of the flying red shards.
Being angry isn't bad. But stealing my mouth and shouting for me—that isn't being on my side.
The red glass fragments trembled in midair, losing speed.
You can be on my side. But not in a way that makes me disappear.
Angry Yeoni's face stiffened. The black shards underfoot melted away. The red light softened, as though folding away its thorns.
“Then... don't just keep holding it in,” Angry Yeoni murmured.
Okay. Next time I'll say it there and then, so I don't end up kicking my blankets. I'll practice.
Angry Yeoni dissolved into red light. The light became a small red mirror shard and quietly settled beside Yeoni.
It has turned toward Friend. You have gained an ally.
Oh. Did I just catch my first Pokémon? Felt like throwing a Poké Ball.
As Yeoni fluttered their hooves excitedly, their flat nostrils puffed out a snort all by themselves. Oink. A pale streak of breath fogged the corridor, then dispersed.
...Do not understand it that way.
They are not Pokémon. They neither run away nor evolve.
But thinking of it that way suddenly makes this feel manageable.
The next to come forward was Giving-up Yeoni. No, not come forward. Still slumped on the floor, that self merely raised its head. Its eyes were empty.
“You don't have to try. It's only going to fail again.”
Yeoni's heart dropped. That voice was too familiar. The exhaustion before even beginning. Nights spent folding hopes away early, afraid hope would only make it hurt more.
“You know it too. The more you hope, the more exhausting it gets.”
...Yeah. I know. Painfully well.
“Then just let it go.” Gray mirror fragments floated around that self. Each reflected a moment when Yeoni had given up.
An application closed just before clicking Submit. A message fully written, then erased. Fingers turning a screen facedown at dawn as though it meant nothing.
“No expectations, no disappointment.” The words were strangely sweet. A promise not to hurt. Yeoni's feet slipped back for a moment.
Then blue ripples curled beneath the flower on their head. The energy of [亥]. Deep water. A heart that might sink, but never quite disappear.
But I... I've given up early to avoid being disappointed so many times.
Giving-up Yeoni slowly raised its head.
It was easier then. For that one moment.
The gray shards trembled like ripples.
But trying and failing hurts for a few days, then ends. Not trying follows me for years. Every time I lie down at night, it comes back.
Giving-up Yeoni's face twisted. “...But it's still scary.”
Yes. I'm scared right now. My hooves are shaking.
But I don't want you folding away my choices just because I'm afraid. If I'm going to fold them away, I'll do it myself.
One by one, the gray shards lost their strength and fell. “Then... what about when it's really hard?”
Then let's rest.
“...Instead of giving up?”
Yes. Resting and giving up. Let's start telling those apart, you and me.
Giving-up Yeoni watched silently for a long time. Then nodded, slowly, very slowly. Gray changed to silver. A small silver shard flew over to join Yeoni.
Your second Friend.
Second... Is this a loyalty card? Collect ten and get a free gift?
Is this really a trial? It feels like paid therapy right now.
The Island of Companions is where you sort through the energies like yourself within you.
Then give the service a softer name. That was practically personal training at a mental gym. And I haven't even paid membership fees.
There are no fees. But neither can you leave halfway through.
Then the reflected Yeoni clapped. Clap. Clap. Clap. Three slow beats.
Touching. I nearly cried.
But tell me. Do you really think all of them can be on your side?
This time, dozens of mirror shards rushed forward at once. Comparing Yeoni. Jealous Yeoni. Forced-smile Yeoni. Yeoni belittling themself.

“They can do it. Why can't you?” “Pretend you're fine. Don't ruin the mood.” “You've always been unlucky.” “Don't get your hopes up.” “Step forward for nothing and you'll only embarrass yourself more.”
Voices poured in from everywhere at once. Yeoni wanted to cover both ears. But their blunt hooves let all the sound through.
Oh, come on! This is a group chat blowing up at three in the morning!
Can't mute it, can't leave. This is mandatory participation!
Of course. They're all you.
The voices swelled. “Compare yourself.” “Hide it.” “Give up.” “Just laugh it off.” “There was never a place for you to begin with.”
The flower on Yeoni's head shook precariously. The green light of [乙] dimmed. Even the ripples of [亥] roiled black.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front and sliced the fragments away. Clang, clang, clang. But they multiplied faster than he could cut them down.
Yeoni, don't fight them one at a time! You'll be buried!
Then what do I do! They all have my face. I don't know where to start!
Set a standard!
A standard? What standard!
The voice that protects you, and the voice that takes you away. Divide them by that alone!
Yeoni caught their breath. The protective voice and the taking voice. Those two phrases clicked together in their mind like a lock.
Suddenly, the mirror shards that had looked identical began to look a little different.
Angry Yeoni had really been shouting for them to speak. Giving-up Yeoni had really been whispering that it was all right to rest.
But Comparing Yeoni kept cutting them smaller. Forced-smile Yeoni erased them from the spot. Self-belittling Yeoni quietly left their chair empty.
Yeoni stamped a hoof firmly into the ground.
Okay. Time to sort this out.
The flower overhead brightened green again.
Those of you trying to protect me, come over here.
Green vines opened a path to Yeoni's right. The red and silver shards settled side by side along it.
And those of you who keep eating away at me—
Yeoni looked straight at the reflection.
Stay exactly where you are.
Hmm. You think you can tell the difference?
I'm starting to get the idea. Can't guarantee my accuracy, though.
What if you're wrong?
Then I'll learn again. Retaking classes is my specialty.
I'm not someone who always chooses perfectly. But now I won't mistake every voice I hear for my own.
With those words, the light of [乙亥] appeared before Yeoni. A green shoot rooted itself upon deep water. The water was dark but clear; the shoot small but firm.
Yeoni reached a hoof toward the light.
No!

The reflected Yeoni swung a hand. The shards of Comparing Yeoni, Forced-smile Yeoni, and Self-belittling Yeoni fused into one mass. A huge hand of black glass was born. It reached to seize all of [乙亥].
Yeoni.
I know. I see it!
Little Sprout, Hang In There! Just three seconds!
...Are you settling on that name?
Names later! This is urgent!
Green vines burst outward and wrapped tightly around the black glass hand. But the hand was too large. The vines stretched taut, creaking as though about to snap.
Yeoni slid backward. Their hooves scraped the floor.
Aagh, is this strength gap real? Somebody patch the balance!
See? You're weak in the end. You always were.
Being weak and losing are completely different things.
The water of [亥] moved. Deep water flowed into the base of the vines and supported their roots from below. The vines thickened, blue seeping into their green light.
Eulhae has connected! Now, Yeoni!
Yeoni slammed their outstretched hoof down with all their strength.
Get out of my place!
The vines constricted the black glass hand. Crack. A hairline split appeared across its back. For the first time, the reflection's face hardened.
Yes, I waver! I admit it!
Crack. Fractures spread like a web.
But me wavering doesn't give you the right to live my life for me!
Crash! The black glass hand shattered. The mirrors of comparison, forced smiles, and self-belittlement broke with it. Their fragments scattered into black dust.
Only a few shards remained. The angry self's red shard. The silver one that said resting was allowed. And a small blue shard, newly born.
...Well done. I mean that.
I really did well, right? Confirm it for me.
Yes. You did well.
Okay. Save this moment. I don't get many scenes like this in life.
Overcome with delight, Yeoni threw up their hooves. Their short hind legs lost balance, and they toppled sideways. The cool pose had lasted exactly three sentences.
Yeongnyangi shook his head silently. Then another message appeared in the center of the corridor.

[ Friend classification complete ]
[ Rob Wealth purification in progress ]
[ Eulhae Day Pillar recovery: 87% ]
Wait. Why isn't it 100%? I just cleared it!
The reflected Yeoni smiled slowly. That self had not disappeared. It stood calmly on the broken mirror fragments, looking down at Yeoni.
Of course.
I'm the final Rob Wealth.
A chill ran down Yeoni's spine. Wings of black mirror spread wide behind the reflection. Every feather held a face.
Faces Yeoni had envied. People they had secretly compared themself to. Selves they wished to become. And the versions of their own face they hated most in the world.
To defeat me, you don't have to break me.
The reflection pointed a fingertip at the center of its chest.
You have to take me back inside you.
...What? What does that mean?
I'm the self you threw away. Destroy me, and part of you disappears too.
Yeoni searched for a rebuttal and found none. Beside them, Yeongnyangi's expression had hardened too.
Yeoni.
...Yes.
This is the true final trial.
Yeoni faced the self in the mirror. A human face. An apparently flawless expression. And curled inside the smile, a force that stole. Rob Wealth.
Okay. So, basically... this is the final boss fight.
Yes. You finally caught on.
The whole island shook again. One final sentence appeared over the corridor.

[ Final Rob Wealth Battle ]
[ Reclaim the self in the mirror. ]
Reclaim. You make it sound so easy.
If you run, it will take your entire place.
Then what if I just fight and smash it?
If all you do is destroy it, you lose part of yourself too.
Then what's the answer? Give me a hint.
...Make it yours. Do not push it away. Embrace it.

Yeoni looked at the reflection for a long time. The reflection looked back in the same way. One human, one flower pig. Completely different faces, yet their eyes resembled each other a little more than before.
I really do make being me difficult.
...You can say that again.
This reply held no mockery. For one brief moment, the blink of an eye, they looked like the same person sharing the same exhaustion.
Then the reflected Yeoni spread its black wings and lunged.
[ Island of Companions · Final Battle Begins ]
